what: rows of cogPG.PG005 displaced to data/corpus_secondary because a served work already carries them
reverse: restore the rows from the witness file to data/corpus/cogPG.PG005.jsonl and delete them there

held_deliberately.why: these three clear the repo's codified FHG gate (>=0.6 with >=20 words) and are NOT shed. Taking a row out of the served corpus is a stronger claim than matching two fragment collections, and this issue already set the standard: PG113 kept Theophylact Simocatta primary at 0.697 because it missed 0.7. At 0.6 a third of the row is not in the work it would be shed against, and that third would leave the corpus.

rows.note: a stitched florilegium row: Polycarp Philippians 13 and then Ignatius. It scores only 0.346 against the served polycarpus.epistula-ad-philippenses, which is not evidence against Eusebius being the right source: that file's chapters 10-14 are Latin transliterated into Greek script, because the Greek of Philippians 13 survives only in Eusebius' quotation of it.
0.739 only on a union of the two Ignatian recensions. The gate is single-source by rule, so a union score does not count.

held_deliberately.if_the_rule_changes: shedding all three would move 1,462 tokens instead of 886. That is a disposition call about how much of a row may be absent from its source before it stops being the same text, not a measurement, and it is cisco's.
